how-it-works.title: How it works
how-it-works.description: How mentoring works at Community Help Co: a free chat, goals set together, then weekly 1:1 online sessions with written notes on progress and next steps.
how-it-works.lede: Simple on purpose. You always know what we're working on and what happens next.

steps.d: Email Simon to set up a short video call about what you want to change and whether we're a good fit. No cost, no commitment.
We turn the bigger picture into small goals you can start on this week, in your words, at your pace.
Each week we check in, celebrate the wins, sort out what got in the way and set the next step. You get written notes after every session.

p: Sessions are one-to-one on Microsoft Teams, from a phone, tablet or computer. Each week we start with what happened since last time: what went well, what got in the way, and how you're feeling about it.

Then we pick the next step. Goals are written in your words and kept small enough to actually do before the next session. If a goal didn't happen, that's useful information, not a failure: we work out why and adjust.

After every session you get a short written summary by email: the goals we set, the wins, anything that got in the way, and the next steps. You can share the notes with family, your support coordinator or your plan manager, or keep them to yourself. Over a few months they become a record of how far you've come.

Week one is the free chat and setting the first goals. Over the next few weeks we settle into a rhythm of weekly sessions and notes. At the end of the first month we look back together at what's working and decide what to focus on next.

You can pay privately (email for current rates), or use NDIS funding if your plan is self-managed or plan-managed. Community Help Co is an unregistered NDIS provider, so sessions can't be paid from NDIA-managed plans.

about.title: About Community Help Co
about.description: Community Help Co is a Melbourne-based mentoring service run by Simon Farrugia, offering online 1:1 life goals and employment support.
paragraphs: Community Help Co is run by me, Simon Farrugia, in Melbourne. I work one-to-one with people who want to get more out of life and work, one week at a time.

My approach is practical. We agree on small, specific goals, you have a go during the week, and we look at what happened together, without judgement. Progress comes from showing up each week, not from big promises.

Sessions are online on Microsoft Teams, so you can join from wherever you're comfortable. After every session you get written notes, so you, your family or your support coordinator can see what we're working on.
We work with private clients and with NDIS participants who are self-managed or plan-managed (Community Help Co is an unregistered NDIS provider). ABN 89 640 199 935.

privacy-policy.title: Privacy policy
privacy-policy.description: How Community Help Co collects, uses and protects your personal information, in line with the Australian Privacy Principles.
paragraphs: Last updated: October 2026. Community Help Co (ABN 89 640 199 935) respects your privacy and handles personal information in line with the Australian Privacy Principles.

What we collect on this website: the details you choose to send in our enquiry or referral forms (name, email, phone if given, who the support is for, the service you're interested in and your message). Please don't include health details, NDIS numbers, dates of birth or addresses in the forms; we'll discuss anything sensitive privately.
How we use it: only to reply to you, arrange a free chat and provide our services. We don't sell or share your details with anyone for marketing.
Getting started: if you email us, we use your email only to reply and arrange a free chat. Sessions run on Microsoft Teams.
Website analytics: we may use privacy-friendly analytics to count visits to pages. It doesn't identify you.
Session notes and client records are stored securely and only shared with your consent (for example with your plan manager or support coordinator).

To see, correct or delete the information we hold about you, or to make a privacy complaint, email simon@communityhelp.com.au. If you're not satisfied with our response, you can contact the Office of the Australian Information Commissioner (oaic.gov.au).

free-daily-journal.title: Free daily gratitude journal
free-daily-journal.description: A free printable gratitude journal: five minutes in the morning, five at night. 90 days of pages, plus journal prompts and daily affirmation ideas. No sign-up.
free-daily-journal.lede: Five minutes in the morning, five at night. 90 days of pages to build a steady habit of gratitude, intention and reflection. Free to download and print, no sign-up.
free-daily-journal.quote: I've been keeping a daily journal for years now, and it has substantially improved my life. This simple structure keeps you focused, grounded, and aligned with your goals.
morning: What will make today great (three actions)

howTo.d: Write three things you're grateful for, three actions that would make today great, and one affirmation. Keep the actions small enough to actually do today.
Note three good things, one lesson and one win, however small. Wins count: a phone call made, a walk taken, a job applied for.
Flick through the last seven days. Patterns jump out: what keeps making days great, and what keeps getting in the way. That's where the next goal comes from.

Gratitude: Who made my life a little easier this week?
What's something I use every day that I'd miss?
What went better than I expected recently?
What's a small moment from yesterday I'd happily repeat?
Intentions: What is one thing that would make today feel worthwhile?
What have I been putting off that would take under ten minutes?
Who could I check in with today?
What would future me thank me for doing today?
Reflection: What gave me energy today, and what drained it?
What did I learn about myself this week?
What's one thing I handled better than I would have a year ago?
What would I do differently tomorrow?

affirmations: I can do hard things, one step at a time.
Small steps every day add up.
I'm allowed to ask for help.
I show up for myself, even on slow days.
My progress counts, even when it's quiet.
I learn from today and start fresh tomorrow.
I'm building a life that feels like mine.
I don't have to be perfect to make progress.

resume-builder.title: Free resume builder
resume-builder.seoTitle: Free Resume Builder (Australia): No Sign-Up, Save as PDF
resume-builder.description: Build a clean Australian-format resume for free. No sign-up, nothing stored: type, check the preview, then save it as a PDF or print it.
resume-builder.lede: Type your details, watch your resume take shape, then save it as a PDF. Free, no sign-up, and what you type never leaves your device.
resume-builder.privacy: Everything you type stays in this browser. Nothing is sent to us or anyone else. Close the page and it's gone, unless you tick “Remember on this device” (don't tick it on a shared or library computer).

tips.about: Use the name you go by at work. A suburb and state is enough: employers don't need your street address, and an Australian resume never needs your date of birth, a photo or your marital status.
tips.summary: Two to four sentences: who you are, what you're good at, and the kind of work you want. Write it last, once the rest is done. Example: “Reliable and friendly team member with two years in hospitality. Calm under pressure and quick to learn new systems. Looking for a retail role with weekend hours.”
tips.skills: List 6 to 10 skills, one per line. Mix practical skills (cash handling, Microsoft Excel, forklift) with how you work (punctual, good with customers). Copy words from the job ad where they're true for you: many employers scan for them.
tips.work: Newest job first. Under each one, add 2 to 4 short lines starting with a doing word: “Served 200+ customers a day”, “Trained three new staff”. Numbers help. Short jobs, casual work and family business count.
tips.gaps: Gaps are normal. If you were caring for family, studying, recovering, volunteering or job hunting, you can say so in one line, or leave it for the interview. You never have to explain health details.
tips.education: Newest first. Include short courses and certificates (TAFE, online courses, a First Aid certificate). If you finished school recently, add your school and the year you finished.
tips.volunteering: Volunteering, community work, sport and helping out in a family business all show real skills. Treat them like jobs: role, organisation, dates and what you did.
tips.licences: Common ones employers look for: driver licence (and if you have a car), Working with Children Check, police check, RSA, RSG, White Card, First Aid, forklift licence.
tips.referees: Most Australian resumes say “Referees available on request”. Ask your referees first, and only share their details when an employer asks.

howTo.d: Start with your details and work history. Use “Fill with an example” to see how a finished one looks.
The resume updates as you type. Pick the Clean or Classic look.
Press “Save as PDF or print”. On a phone or computer, choose “Save as PDF” as the printer. Then attach it to job applications.

faq.q: What format do Australian employers expect?
faq.a: Two pages is the usual length (one is fine if you're starting out). Your name and contact details at the top, a short summary, then skills, work history (newest first), education and licences. No photo, no date of birth, and referees “available on request”.

faq.q: I've never had a job. What do I put?
faq.a: Lead with your skills and summary, then education, volunteering, school leadership, sport, babysitting, helping in a family business, or anything where you turned up and did the work. Employers hiring for first jobs look for reliability and attitude more than experience.

faq.q: Is it really free? Where does my information go?
faq.a: It's free, with no sign-up and no ads. The resume is built inside your browser, so we never see what you type. We only count page visits.

faq.q: Should I change my resume for each job?
faq.a: Yes, a little. Keep one main version, then tweak the summary and skills to match the words in each job ad.

faq.q: Can someone help me with my job search?
faq.a: Yes. Job Catalyst is Community Help Co's 1:1 job coaching: resumes, applications, interview practice and staying on track. Email Simon for a free chat.
